preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain control of the owner address)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, call setMarketinWalleAddress() to set the marketing wallet to attacker's address, then trigger swapAndLiquify to collect accumulated BNB fees. Alternatively, use changeRouterVeslon() if you control the ________ address to mint massive tokens, or use qwidji() to blacklist users and block their transactions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has multiple owner privilege vulnerabilities: 1) The owner can set the marketing wallet address via setMarketinWalleAddress(), 2) The owner can call changeRouterVeslon() if they control the ________ address to mint massive tokens, 3) The owner can use qwidji() to blacklist users. The most direct economic exploit is to become owner, set marketing wallet to attacker address, and trigger swapAndLiquify to collect accumulated BNB fees from the contract.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank() 2. Call setMarketinWalleAddress() to set marketing wallet to attacker address 3. Generate some fee accumulation by making trades 4. Trigger swapAndLiquify to collect BNB fees
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner (we need to find the owner address first) 2. Call setMarketinWalleAddress(attacker) to redirect marketing fees 3. Buy some tokens to generate fees that accumulate in contract 4. Sell tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify (which sends BNB to marketing wallet) 5. Verify attacker's BNB balance increased
